title: Comparison of laser enucleation of the prostate in benign prostatic hyperplasia with versus without the HoloLase MD glasses – a prospective randomized study
summary:
Many men experience benign enlargement of the prostate gland as they age. This can lead to difficulty urinating, frequent urges to urinate, or incomplete bladder emptying. If medication is insufficient, surgery to remove prostate tissue is often necessary. For many years, this procedure has been performed safely and successfully using laser energy via the urethra without an external incision.

Until now, the surgeon has viewed the surgical image on a screen. A new type of special glasses has been developed that projects the surgical image directly into the surgeon's field of vision (HoloLase MD glasses). This is intended to improve posture and potentially make the procedure faster. However, whether this new technique actually offers advantages and is as safe as the conventional screen-based display has not yet been sufficiently investigated.

The aim of this study is to compare both approaches. It will examine whether the procedure can be performed more efficiently with the glasses without increasing the risk of complications or compromising patient outcomes. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: In one group, the operation is performed using conventional screen display, while in the other group, it is performed with the aid of the new glasses. The operation itself is identical in both groups. Complaints, recovery, and any potential side effects are recorded before and after the procedure. The study will not result in any additional procedures or burdens for participants beyond their regular treatment.

interventions.name: The patients receive the novel HoLEP surgical procedure with visualization via HoloLase MD glasses (intervention group).
The patients receive the conventional HoLEP surgical procedure with monitor visualization (observation group).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for laser enucleation of the prostate and signed informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Prostate volume less than or equal to 30 cc
- Urethral stricture
- Preoperative confirmation or indication of prostate cancer
- Confirmed neurogenic bladder dysfunction
